validated_strengths: Both author seals and every sealed file entry verify exactly; docs/359 remains unchanged.
Independent raw M40/M158 event reconstruction exactly reproduces all 126 ordered descriptors, including eight negative tuples and both destination halves.
Independent M41 checkpoint addressing reproduces every exported INT8 weight byte, and an independent integer oracle covers 504 updates and 4,032 lanes without signed19 overflow.
Dense high-half addressing is correct: local row 303 maps to 687 rather than the erroneous concatenation address 815.
M149, M154 and M155 are not instantiated; the accumulator same-address forwarding payload is absent by construction, while lazy-valid state and all-bank overflow write suppression remain.
The reported 56 macro reads plus 448 cache hits and 9.0x read-work ratio are arithmetically correct and explicitly fenced from cycle, energy and system claims.

P1.title: Weight and accumulator macro timing is a hard-coded one-cycle assumption
P1.evidence: Neither memory interface has response-valid, response tag or backpressure. The sealed TB uses one-cycle synchronous behavioral arrays. Independent VCS returns the correct +10 with one-cycle weight latency but returns stale 0 instead of +11 with two-cycle latency.
P1.impact: The island is not latency-elastic and cannot yet be connected to a selected SRAM compiler point. The 9.0x cache number is read work, not cycle reduction, and no-forward II=1 is conditional on the exact one-cycle macro recurrence.
P1.required_action: Bind exact weight and Acc19 macro timing/width/ports or add response-valid plus context/order tags and elastic holding. Replay one-, two- and stalled-response cases before cycle admission.

P1.title: The executable workload scope is one opportunistic 8-lane context, not the finite M152 chain
P1.evidence: The exact run covers sample 5, operator 0, partition 251, window 7, 126 all-full4 descriptors and only 8 of 96 lanes. M152 descriptorization, final scan/requantization and the complete four-operator trace remain external; no explicit window identity is carried by the RTL.
P1.impact: The local exactness result does not establish full96 behavior, real tail distribution, four-layer recurrence, finite load/close overhead or window replay safety.
P1.required_action: Add an explicit window/context identity, connect the complete M152 finite trace adapter, and run full96 exact VCS across all four bottleneck operators and heldout samples, including naturally occurring tails.

P1.title: M238's 1.687018x remains an uncalibrated cycle-model target
P1.evidence: Independent arithmetic reproduces 126,581,635 / 75,032,786 = 1.687017659x, but M241 measures neither baseline nor candidate cycles on the complete trace. It also has no matched M155 forwarding versus no-forward DC/STA, SRAM macro PPA, SAIF or PTPX.
P1.impact: Removing the 7,296-bit accumulator forwarding payload may be offset by cache, pipeline, interlock, overflow and macro costs. No achieved module throughput, area-throughput or energy advantage exists yet.
P1.required_action: Run the same finite trace through matched forwarding/no-forward RTL with identical SRAM macros and load/commit charges; then perform same-library DC/STA and activity-based energy.

P1.title: Numeric overflow suppresses memory writes but still handshakes commit
P1.evidence: commit_valid is assigned directly from s2_valid_q and is not gated by s2_overflow_any. Independent VCS observes overflow_error=1, all acc_wr_en=0 and commit_accept=1 in the same failing transaction. The sealed production test checks write suppression but deliberately has no younger token in flight and does not reject the completion handshake.
P1.impact: A downstream consumer can count an update as completed although no accumulator write occurred. The accepted-younger quarantine/abort contract is also invisible outside the island, so fault-atomic integration is not closed.
P1.required_action: Either suppress commit on overflow or add an explicit fault/abort completion type and acknowledged context flush. Test overflow with accepted younger s0/s1 tokens, commit stalls and exact downstream accounting.

P1.title: Checkpoint epoch is caller metadata, not a bound macro-response identity
P1.evidence: The physical weight address is only {half,source}; partition, operator, epoch and window do not travel to the external macro response. The production 'cache epoch alias' attack is a wrong descriptor epoch rejected against context metadata, not a stale loader/macro response with a matching caller epoch.
P1.impact: A stale or misloaded 32x96x8 resident bank can be consumed while all internal tag comparisons pass. 'Checkpoint-tagged' is safe only as an internal cache-key statement, not an end-to-end checkpoint-data guarantee.
P1.required_action: Add loader completion and payload-epoch identity to context open, or return a checked macro response tag. Attack stale contents, delayed prior-context responses and same-epoch/wrong-operator reloads.

P2.title: Real tail coverage is absent
P2.detail: All 126 real descriptors are full4. Four directed prefix tails use real partition weights, while the overflow stress creates many repetitive single-bank tails; neither substitutes for naturally distributed finite-trace tails.

P2.title: The removed payload is not yet a measured net storage reduction
P2.detail: M241 removes M155's named 7,296-bit accumulator forwarding payload but introduces production-width cache_data, s0_hit_data, s1_delta and s2_delta state. Only matched synthesis can establish net FF/area/fanout reduction.

P2.title: The accumulator macro is exceptionally wide
P2.detail: At LANES=96 each of four Acc19 banks exposes a 1,824-bit read and 1,824-bit write vector per address; each weight bank exposes 768 bits. Compiler availability, banking/striping and wire timing are unspecified.

P2.title: No Formality or mapped-netlist tie exists
P2.detail: M241 has exact RTL VCS but no DC point or RTL-to-netlist Formality receipt. This is acceptable for the present milestone and blocks paper PPA.

P2.title: M149 bypass is proven structurally, not as a system delta
P2.detail: The selected island correctly does not instantiate M149, but it also does not instantiate M154/M155 or a matched parent. Area and cycle savings from the bypass cannot yet be added to prior logic-only points.

allowed_claims: Under an exact one-cycle behavioral SRAM contract, M241 is an 8-lane four-bank standalone INT8-to-Acc19 island that passes a 126-descriptor real ordered subset with 504 exact writes and 4,032 lane checks at zero mismatch.
Independent reconstruction confirms eight real negative tuples, 63 low-half and 63 high-half descriptors, zero adjacent bank/address aliases in the selected subset, and dense high-half address 687.
The selected subset performs 56 weight macro reads and 448 cache hits, a 9.0x reduction in weight-read work only.
M241 removes the named accumulator same-address forwarding payload by construction and uses a one-entry same-address interlock while retaining lazy-valid and overflow write suppression.
The M238 value 1.687017659x is a same-PWP1024 cycle-model target that M241 does not admit.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim 9.0x or 1.687018x as achieved cycle speedup, throughput, energy efficiency or system speedup.
Do not claim the current interface is compatible with arbitrary or two-cycle SRAM macros, or that no-forward II=1 has been proved with a selected physical macro.
Do not claim full96, complete four-operator trace, natural-tail, PAFT, full-network or paper-PPA coverage.
Do not claim numeric-overflow completion is transaction-atomic until commit/abort semantics and accepted-younger behavior are repaired and tested.
Do not claim a measured 7,296-bit net storage, area or power reduction versus M155 before matched synthesis.
next_gates: Repair or explicitly type overflow commit/abort semantics and cover accepted-younger overflow plus stalled completion.
Bind checkpoint loader and macro-response identity, including explicit window context.
Select weight and accumulator SRAM macros, close exact response latency/width, or make both return paths elastic and tagged.
Run full96 VCS on the complete M152 finite ordered trace for all four bottleneck operators and heldout samples with real tails.
Run matched M155-forwarding versus M241-no-forward DC/STA with identical macro cuts, then calibrate the cycle simulator and measure SAIF/PTPX energy.
